Story / Service before spectacle

Service before spectacle

Build for people. Stay useful.

Military service, community leadership, overseas intelligence and technology work, and mental-health advocacy all shaped the same operating principle: make the work practical, humane, and accountable.

01

Military and overseas work

Service changed how I understand systems and responsibility.

I served in the United States Air Force and later worked with military-adjacent organizations, international teams, and intelligence and technology contractors around the world. The public version of that history stays deliberately high level: the lasting lesson is that technical choices always land on real people.

Professional timelineCareer and education context on LinkedInOpen source ↗
02

Veterans and mental health

Support should feel human before it feels institutional.

My advocacy centers practical tools, community, and honest conversations that respect lived experience—especially for veterans navigating transition, isolation, and mental-health challenges. I care about technology that lowers friction without pretending software can replace human care.

AI Nerd video archiveOpen-source AI and Veteran LifeLine workOpen source ↗
03

Rotary and RYLA

Leadership is something people practice together.

I have worked closely with Rotary and Rotary Youth Leadership Awards communities. Their emphasis on service, ethical leadership, and developing young people fits the same pattern I value in open source: share responsibility, make room for others, and leave a system stronger.
